title: Copyright Legislation Amendment (Fair Go for Fair Use) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would introduce a flexible fair use exception to copyright law, widen service provider protections and change rules for digital locks and geographic restrictions.
It would extend safe harbour arrangements beyond carriage service providers and permit visually impaired people and assisting institutions to bypass locks on lawfully purchased content.
The changes would begin the day after Royal Assent and address geographic controls that prevent Australians accessing legitimately acquired content or impose different prices.
changes: A broader service provider definition would cover online services, network access and data transmission facilities.
Public and non-profit institutions’ copyright responsibilities would recognise limits on responsibility for users’ behaviour.
The existing section 200AB exception would be repealed and a new fair use provision inserted.
summary.affected: Visually impaired people, Australian consumers, educational and cultural institutions, libraries, service providers and copyright creators and holders are affected.
